overview.description: Bonanza Pai Gow is a casino variant of standard Chinese Pai Gow dominoes that adds two side bets â€” a Bonus bet and a Tie bet â€” alongside the traditional main wager. Played on a standard blackjack-sized table for up to 6 players, it uses Chinese dominoes, three dice, and chips. The core gameplay remains standard Pai Gow (form high and low hands from 4 tiles), but the extra betting circles make every hand a decision point, and pushes â€” which occur ~40% of the time in standard Pai Gow â€” generate payouts on the side bets.
overview.origin: Australia (commercialised variant of Chinese Pai Gow)

history.origins: Bonanza Pai Gow was created by Gambology and copyrighted as a casino table game. It is a modification of traditional Chinese Pai Gow that adds Bonus and Tie side bets. The game was introduced at Crown Casino in Melbourne, Australia in January 2001.
timeline: Traditional: Chinese Pai Gow has been played for centuries with 32 dominoes.
January 2001: Bonanza Pai Gow introduced at Crown Casino, Melbourne, Australia.
June 2001: All 6 of Crown Casino's standard Pai Gow tables had been converted to Bonanza Pai Gow due to its increased hold percentage.
Present: Available in select casinos; Gambology's original website no longer exists.
history.evolution: Bonanza Pai Gow solves the core commercial problem with standard Pai Gow: the ~40% push rate frustrates players and limits casino revenue. By adding the Tie bet (which specifically rewards pushes) and the Bonus bet (which triggers every ~3.7 hands), every hand produces a betting decision and a result.
history.cultural: Pai Gow is deeply rooted in Chinese gambling culture. The Bonanza variant represents the modernisation of traditional games for the Western casino floor, optimising for player engagement and house revenue simultaneously.

setup.players: 1 to 6 players, each playing against the Banker (house or rotating player-banker).
setup.deck: Chinese domino set: 32 tiles arranged in 16 pairs. Each tile has a specific ranking in the Pai Gow system.
setup.equipment: Chinese domino set. Three dice (for determining deal order). Blackjack-sized table with three betting circles per player: main bet (seat number), Bonus bet ('B'), and Tie bet ('T').
setup.dealing: Tiles are shuffled and stacked. Three dice are rolled to determine dealing order. Each player and the banker receive 4 tiles.

rules.objective: Form two hands (high hand and low hand) from your 4 tiles that both beat the Banker's corresponding hands.
rules.gameplay: Each player receives 4 tiles and must split them into a High Hand (2 tiles) and a Low Hand (2 tiles). The High Hand must rank at least equal to the Low Hand according to standard Pai Gow tile rankings. After all players have set their hands, the Banker reveals their 4 tiles and forms their high and low hands.
keyRules: High Hand must rank â‰¥ Low Hand (standard Pai Gow rule).
Main bet: win both = win, lose both = lose, split = push.
Bonus bet: pays on hand strength independent of banker.
Tie bet: pays on push outcomes.
Main bet is NOT mandatory â€” players can play Bonus and/or Tie bets alone.
House edge on Bonus and Tie bets doesn't change whether players bank or not.

strategy.basic: Learn the standard Pai Gow tile ranking system. Set your hands according to the house way (standard optimal splitting). The side bets are independent decisions â€” the Bonus bet has moderate hit frequency, the Tie bet capitalises on the high push rate.
strategy.intermediate: In standard Pai Gow, the house edge is significantly reduced when players take turns banking. However, Bonanza Pai Gow's Bonus and Tie bets have FIXED house edges regardless of who banks â€” making them purely house-advantage bets.
strategy.advanced: Optimal main-bet strategy: bank whenever possible (standard Pai Gow advice). Side-bet strategy: the Bonus bet's ~27% hit rate (every 3.7 hands) provides frequent wins with moderate variance. The Tie bet exploits the ~40% push rate but typically has a higher house edge. Calculate expected value for each bet independently.
tips: The regular bet is optional â€” some players skip it entirely and play only side bets.
Bonus bet hits every ~3.7 hands: steady wins, but payouts may not overcome house edge long-term.
Tie bet capitalises on the frustrating ~40% push rate of standard Pai Gow.
Banking doesn't affect Bonus/Tie house edges, only the main bet.

considerations: 32 unique tiles with complex ranking system requires specialised knowledge base.
Three independent betting decisions per hand multiply the strategy space.
Side-bet EV calculation requires fixed paytable analysis.
Banking rotation affects only main bet â€” AI must track this separately.
Push probability (~40%) significantly affects risk/reward of all bets.

edgeCases.text: Banker wins all ties when the highest-ranking tiles in the hand also tie.
When both player and Banker low hands total 0, the Banker wins the low hand.
Player sets their hand once; the same setting is used to adjudicate both the main bet and the Tie bet.
Bonus bet is paid regardless of how the player sets high and low hands when they also have a main bet.

customActions.description: Place a wager in the circle with the seat number; standard Pai Gow bet against the Banker. Win both hands to win; lose both to lose; one win and one lose pushes.
customActions.constraints: Optional; table min and max apply per circle. Player may skip main and play only Bonus or Tie.

customActions.description: Place a wager in the circle labeled B. Player wins if their four tiles form one of eight Bonus hands (e.g. Supreme Pair and Heaven Pair 200:1, Lame Duck 20:1, Wong 1:1); does not compete against the Banker.
customActions.constraints: Optional; table limits apply. Pays on hand composition regardless of how hands are set.

customActions.description: Place a wager in the circle labeled T. Player wins if their hand ties the Banker (even money, or 25:1/20:1 if low hand is at least a Gong).
customActions.constraints: Optional; same hand setting used for main and Tie adjudication.

customActions.description: Do not place the regular Pai Gow bet; player may still place Bonus and Tie bets.
customActions.constraints: Legal when player chooses not to wager on the main bet.

customActions.description: Roll three dice to determine dealing order for the round.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; performed at start of deal phase.

customActions.description: Shuffle the 32-tile set and deal four tiles to each player and the Banker in order determined by the dice.
Form two hands from four tiles: a High Hand (two tiles) and a Low Hand (two tiles). High Hand must rank at least equal to Low Hand per Pai Gow tile rankings.
customActions.constraints: Each player sets once; same setting used for main and Tie bet resolution.

customActions.description: Banker reveals their four tiles and forms High Hand and Low Hand according to house way or optimal setting.
customActions.constraints: System or dealer; after all players have set.

customActions.description: Compare each player's High Hand to the Banker's High Hand using Pai Gow tile rankings; ties broken by highest-ranking tile, then Banker wins.
Compare each player's Low Hand to the Banker's Low Hand; when both low hands total 0, Banker wins the low hand.
Resolve main bet: win both hands pays 1:1 minus commission; lose both loses bet; one win one lose pushes.
customActions.constraints: System; after high and low comparison.

customActions.description: Resolve Bonus bet per paytable (Supreme+Heaven 200:1 down to Wong 1:1); no commission. Paid regardless of hand setting if player also had main bet.
Resolve Tie bet: when player hand ties Banker hand, Tie bettors win even money or 25:1/20:1 for Gong or better on low.
customActions.constraints: System; when player hand ties Banker hand.

engine.handRankingSystem: Standard Pai Gow tile rankings for high and low hands; comparison uses Pai Gow tile hierarchy; ties broken by highest-ranking tile (Banker wins if tiles tie).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 32-tile Chinese domino set. The set has 32 tiles with two ends each showing pip patterns; no Western playing cards. Used for Pai Gow (and Bonanza variant) where tiles are arranged into two hands (front and back) and compared against the banker.
engine.suitDescription: Chinese dominoes do not use Western suits; tiles are grouped by pip pattern and pair types (civil and military). Matching and ranking follow Pai Gow rules; each tile has a rank for the front and back hand comparison.
engine.rankDescription: Tiles are ranked for Pai Gow comparison; the 32-tile set has fixed rankings for making the two hands (front must rank lower than back). No single linear rank; the combination of tiles determines the hand value.
engine.dealPattern: Four tiles each to every player and the banker; deal order determined by three dice.

synthesis.shortDescription: A casino variant of Chinese Pai Gow dominoes that adds Bonus and Tie side bets to every hand. Introduced at Crown Casino Melbourne in 2001, it solved Pai Gow's ~40% push-frustration problem by making pushes pay. Three betting circles per player, main bet optional, every hand a decision.

scoring.splitRules: Push on main bet when one hand wins and one loses.
